chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: concerning

Regarding a man who pushed another man onto a man and he killed him, he said: “The diyyah is upon the one who fell upon the man and killed him, for the heirs of the slain.” He said: “And the one who was pushed may recover the diyyah from the one who pushed him.” He said: “And if anything happens to the one who was pushed, that also is upon the pusher.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: There is no contradiction between this report and the first two reports, because the first two reports dealt with one who slipped and fell upon another, so nothing of the diyyah was binding upon him. As for the last report, the diyyah was only made obligatory in it because the push was not by mistake, but rather was deliberate, so the pusher is liable in accordance with what has been set out in the report.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the legal heirs of the slain person entitled to compensation
key_terms.الدَّافِعِ: the one who did the pushing
key_terms.اَلدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for unlawful killing or injury

ai.seo_question: Who is liable for the diyyah if someone pushes a person onto another and that causes death?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability when a person intentionally pushes someone onto another person, resulting in death. It distinguishes deliberate pushing from accidental slipping, assigning financial liability in a way that ultimately returns responsibility to the intentional pusher.
